text: According to the chapter, an argument is *valid* exactly when:
choices: all of its premises are true
the conclusion is true in every model in which all the premises are true
it is valid and, in addition, all of its premises are true
the conclusion happens to be true in the actual world
explanation: Validity means the conclusion is true in every model where all premises are true; it is a property of form, not of actual truth. Options 1 and 4 confuse validity with having true premises or a true conclusion, and option 3 is the definition of soundness (validity PLUS true premises), not validity.
